body: It was great being able to use it for convenience store runs from my very first day there. Linking adds a discount too, so I was happy to get 10,000 won a little cheaper✨

On the night I arrived, being able to pay for tea and water with a single barcode at the CU near my hotel was more than anything else just easy.
At my age I'm not especially good with phones, but even so I used it without getting lost, which was reassuring.
Linking JPYC adds a discount, so you can get 10,000 won for a little less. There's no bother counting exchanged cash either, so walking around with a light wallet was comfortable.
During my stay I used it every time I stopped at a convenience store, and in the end I used it up neatly. Some points came back too, and at my age I appreciate the way these things add up😊

Traveling with a child, I didn't want to fumble at the register, so I went with CU's 10,000 won voucher. Linking JPYC gets you a small discount, and paying is just holding up your phone. Being able to grab snacks and drinks for my child quickly gave me a lot more breathing room😊
One barcode at the register and I used up 10,000 won at a CU there. Linking added a discount too, and I worked through it on drinks and cup noodles👍

I wanted just the right amount for convenience stores, so I got CU's 10,000 won voucher at a good price by linking JPYC. Only the linking part confused me a little at first, but once I tried it, it was done in a few minutes. It wasn't something to brace yourself for. What prompted me was a post I saw on X, and I got ready for my September trip to Korea. Once I arrived, I paid at convenience stores with just my phone. I could use it freely on drinks and snacks, and it went more smoothly than I imagined😊
